column1: # Released catalogue designs: slug <TAB> version <TAB> content fingerprint <TAB> claims fingerprint.
# Patterns are software releases. The content fingerprint is CIR.fingerprint (the design
# content hash the release chain and the certificate's content hash are taken over, CIR.to_dict)
# with the version blanked, so it measures content alone. The claims fingerprint is
# gates.certificate.claims_fingerprint over the twin block a certificate carries -- finished
# size, polygon spans, yardage and its tolerance -- because a model change that moves a figure
# the buyer reads is a content change even when the CIR is unchanged.
# tests/test_release_versions.py fails when either changes while the version does not.
# HOW TO UPDATE: when you change a design's content or a figure it states, bump that builder's
# default version (a new minor, e.g. 1.1.0 -> 1.2.0) AND update its row's version and both
# fingerprints together in the same commit. Print the current rows with:
# Never update a fingerprint without bumping the version: that is exactly the change this
# table exists to refuse (a buyer's "1.0.0" and a new download's "1.0.0" being different).
# The runtime refuses the same thing at certification (runtime.pipeline handle_certify, PT-03).
# History: a8ed44f (FB3-G, D-FB-6) re-derived gauge and counts; every design whose content
# changed moved 1.0.0 -> 1.1.0. 2026-10-06 (PT-07 yardage counted per stitch once, PT-08
# stitch-weighted row height, PT-09 Cloudline two-row stripes and truthful colour-change notes,
# PT-10 hexagon spans and titles): every design whose content or stated figures changed moved
# one minor (1.1.0 -> 1.2.0; autumn-oak and pebble-raglan 1.0.0 -> 1.1.0). Unchanged:
